question: According to press reports, the anxiolytic drug Pregabalin is spreading in the United Kingdom and has been linked to several fatal accidents and various debilitating side effects. In Great Britain, there were 3 400 deaths linked to the effects of the drug, which is reportedly already prescribed to more than 8 million people.

The side effects are said to be extremely severe, ranging from changes in mood to memory problems and total dependence. Given this drug’s very serious side effects and the potential fatal effects, can the Commission say how it intends to monitor the spread of this drug, and its worrying side effects, in the European Union?
answer: All medicines in the EU are subject to strict post-marketing surveillance with obligations on marketing authorisation holders and competent authorities set by the legislation.

Since the authorisation of the first medicine containing pregabalin, the European Medicines Agency’s Pharmacovigilance Risk Assessment Committee (1) (PRAC) has recommended several updates of the product information to include new safety warnings regarding the possible risks related to the use of these medicines. In 2021, PRAC recommended the inclusion of parkinsonism as a new pregabalin adverse drug reactio n (2).

In 2022, an update to the information related to the risk of abuse and dependence in patients without a history of substance disorde r (3); and in 2023, the addition of information related to suicidal ideation and behaviour after pregabalin withdrawal (4). The generic marketing authorisation holders have also followed the changes for the originator pregabalin.
PRAC will continue to monitor the safety of medicines containing pregabalin to ensure a high level of public health protection in the EU.
